requirements.value: Refunds: replace paper records and phone approvals; cut the average time from refund request to payout from 10 days to 3 days; no refund request is lost and every request is visible to the customer; branch managers decide on their own branch's refunds in one place (REFUNDS 01 Business Objectives 1 to 3). The complaint and portal-share targets of objectives 4 and 5 are open in the BRD. Loyalty: members trust their points balance, measured as zero upheld balance complaints a month (LOYALTY 01 Objective 1, LOYALTY/NFR-01), and check their points without calling a branch (LOYALTY 01 Objective 2, targets open in the BRD).
requirements.evidence: REFUNDS 01: customers wait up to 10 days today; 18% of complaints to customer care are about slow or lost refunds.
requirements.confirmed_by: Policy: test-run policy (set by Product Owner (fixture owner), 2026-10-27)

requirements.label: Customer refund journey (REFUNDS UC-01 to UC-03)
requirements.value: The customer proves who they are, enters a branch receipt number, picks the items and a reason, submits the refund request, follows it until the money is back on the card, and cancels it while it is Submitted. Failure impact: a lost request or a customer without status, the cause of 18% of complaints to customer care (REFUNDS 01).
requirements.confirmed_by: Policy: test-run policy (set by Product Owner (fixture owner), 2026-10-27)

requirements.label: Branch manager decision and payout journey (REFUNDS UC-04)
requirements.value: The branch manager decides on each Submitted request of their branch, oldest first: approve in full or in part, or reject with a reason; an approved refund is paid to the customer's original card through the payment provider and the request becomes Paid. Failure impact: refund money lost or paid twice (REFUNDS/NFR-01).
requirements.confirmed_by: Policy: test-run policy (set by Product Owner (fixture owner), 2026-10-27)

requirements.label: Member points journey (LOYALTY UC-01, UC-02)
requirements.value: The member signs in, sees the points balance with the date of the last movement, and opens the history of points movements and the purchase or refund behind each. Failure impact: members call branches about points and lose trust in the balance (LOYALTY 01).
requirements.confirmed_by: Policy: test-run policy (set by Product Owner (fixture owner), 2026-10-27)

requirements.value: In scope: online refund requests for branch purchases; customers follow and cancel their own requests; branch manager decisions in full or in part; payout to the original card; customer messages by email and SMS; refund outcomes sent to Loyalty Points; a daily refund report per branch manager (REFUNDS 04). calculations.label: Average business TPS
calculations.limitations: Daily average is not peak or burst demand.

calculations.label: Peak business TPS
calculations.limitations: Peak multiplier requires measured demand curve or agreed forecast.

calculations.label: Peak API RPS
calculations.limitations: API calls, event fanout and retries must not be double-counted.

calculations.label: Headroom throughput budget
calculations.limitations: Throughput envelope, not number of nodes. Requires P99 load tests.

calculations.label: Mean requests in flight
calculations.limitations: Little’s Law uses mean latency, not P99 or logged-in users.

calculations.label: Peak inbound network
calculations.limitations: One selected network boundary; excludes replication/east-west flows.

calculations.label: Peak outbound network
calculations.limitations: Directional egress is not a separate guaranteed link rating.

calculations.label: Combined modeled boundary traffic
calculations.limitations: Sum of directional traffic; not a physical link-speed requirement.

calculations.label: Daily API payload transfer
calculations.limitations: Decimal GB; excludes internal and replication traffic.

calculations.label: New logical data per day
calculations.limitations: Assumes every transaction contributes its stated logical size.

calculations.label: Retained logical data
calculations.limitations: Steady-state simplified model; excludes historical growth and erasure.

calculations.label: Planning storage footprint
calculations.limitations: Provider redundancy, snapshots, WAL, logs and backups are not fully modeled.

calculations.label: 30-day downtime budget
calculations.limitations: Calendar-time assumption; SLA exclusions may differ.

calculations.label: Annual downtime budget
calculations.limitations: SLO downtime budget is not an outage-specific RTO.

calculations.label: Hypothetical RPO exposure
calculations.limitations: Potential exposure if peak persisted; not the number of lost committed writes.

calculations.label: One-year projected peak API RPS
calculations.limitations: Simple uniform growth scenario; not an adopted business forecast.

calculations.label: Ideal migration bulk transfer
calculations.limitations: Only bulk-copy lower bound: excludes transform, CDC, verification and rollback.

calculations.label: Proposed address block count
calculations.limitations: Planning block only; no CIDR allocation. Per-provider reserved subnet addresses and IPAM need confirmation.

calculations.label: Estimated business read TPS
calculations.limitations: Assumes read fraction applies to business transactions; not DB query rate.

calculations.label: Estimated business write TPS

diagrams.summary: Primary + independent recovery location candidate, Relational transactional store. RTO 4 h; RPO 15 min; scope region. All nodes and links are proposed logical candidates, not verified deployment facts. Source of product use cases remains the BRD. Required validation: Confirm region/site and actual fault-domain independence; do not infer region or zone availability. | Benchmark compute and data tier throughput under peak and impaired-zone load. | Confirm database durability, failover behavior, backups, IAM, monitoring, and provider eligibility.

Region/VPC(or VNet)/private app and data segments. Trust boundaries, zones/subnets and public/private paths are provisional. Actual IPAM, public subnet associations, provider-managed interfaces, routing and firewall rules must be verified. Required validation: Confirm real CIDR/IPAM allocations, public/private subnet eligibility, zone placement, routes, DNS and security/firewall rules; no IP addresses are assigned here. | Provider networking differs: AWS VPCs regional with AZ subnets; GCP VPCs global with regional subnets; Azure VNets regional. Managed service resources may live on provider-owned boundaries. | Confirm public or private ingress, internet egress/NAT and private endpoint eligibility, independent availability zone paths, and hybrid/partner failover before SDD. | Verify physically independent recovery network and provider/region/site boundaries. Active-active servicing does not ensure zero client-visible failover time.

Failure scope: region; RTO=4 h; RPO=15 min; candidate: Pilot Light. These are targets, NOT achieved results. Required validation: Define recovery critical path: detection → failover authorization → data promotion/restore → app/IAM connectivity → routing → business verification. | Demonstrate application-level recovery, data consistency, dependency reattachment, failback and split-brain protections. | Document separate recovery objective for every in-scope failure scenario, including cyber/data corruption where relevant.

Only technical data paths are proposed here; product entities, use cases and APIs must come from BRDs. Required validation: Confirm authoritative data owners, transaction boundaries, query patterns, mutation/replay semantics and supported cross-region consistency. | Do not infer product schemas or event names.

Network trust boundaries are logical; identity provider, data classification and compliance controls need owner validation. Required validation: Validate authentication/authorization ownership from BRD and architecture questionnaire. | Review segmentation, encryption, key recovery, sensitive data location, audit/retention and source-to-target trust.
